name: CapCut Eye Power Overlay Alignment
use_when: An anime, game, or stylized action edit needs an eye, symbol, aura, or power detail to transform on a beat.
The source clip can be slowed or speed-adjusted enough to align the overlay without destroying action readability.
A character close-up needs a specific identity or power cue rather than whole-frame glow.
avoid_when: The eye or detail is too small, blurred, occluded, or moving too fast for a clean overlay.
The overlay asset is unlicensed, low resolution, or stylistically mismatched.
A whole-frame effect communicates the beat more clearly than a tiny tracked detail.

timeline_pattern.pattern: beat_marker -> source_clip_speed_adjust -> eye_overlay_import -> scale_position_mask -> preview_alignment -> reverse_or_extend_if_needed -> pre_render -> main_timeline_replace -> power_sfx
timeline_pattern.speed_rule: Adjust speed before detailed overlay work so the eye or power detail can be aligned to both the beat and the visible feature.
timeline_pattern.alignment_rule: Review the overlay through the full movement range, not only on the best still frame.
timeline_pattern.replacement_rule: Pre-render or replace only after the overlay lands on the intended beat and the clip duration is stable.

motion.rule: The overlay should follow the character feature closely enough to read as part of the shot, then clear or cut away before drift is visible.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: For a transformation beat, aim for the overlay reveal or lock point to land within 1-2 frames of the target beat when practical.
keyframe_values.hold: Hold the transformed detail only long enough for the viewer to register it before the next motion or transition competes.
keyframe_values.review_range: Check the frames before and after the reveal because eye overlays often fail on approach or exit frames.

sound.rule: Use a short power, zap, eye, or identity cue only on the reveal/lock frame, and keep longer voice lines for character identity beats.

captions.rule: Do not place captions over the eye, face, or power symbol during the transformation beat.

color.rule: Match glow, contrast, and brightness so the overlay feels integrated without washing out the face or expression.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use setpts for speed adjustment, overlay the eye asset with scale/position expressions or tracked metadata, apply alpha/mask edges, then mix a cue with adelay and afade.
implementation.remotion: Store beatFrame, featureCenterByFrame, overlayAsset, playbackRate, revealFrame, clearFrame, and sfxFrame; drive the overlay from those values.
implementation.blender: Track the eye/detail in the compositor or VSE, attach the overlay plane, mask/feather the edges, and render a short intermediate if the stack is heavy.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use Speed to create an alignable moment, add the eye/power overlay above the clip, scale and position it, mask or blend as needed, reverse/extend only if it smooths the beat, export/re-import after timing is approved, then place the SFX.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Time Remapping, a nested overlay layer, opacity masks or tracking, Lumetri/glow matching, Render and Replace for dense sections, and markers for the transformation cue.

common_mistakes: Adding the overlay before the clip speed and beat alignment are known.
Judging the overlay on one paused frame and missing drift during playback.
Leaving the overlay visible after it has stopped matching the eye or symbol.
Using a bright overlay that erases facial expression or action readability.
Baking the effect before preserving a revision path to the source clip.
qc: Does the overlay reveal or lock frame land on the intended beat?
Does the overlay stay aligned through the full visible movement range?
Can the viewer still read the face, expression, and action at phone size?
Are captions clear of the eye, face, or power detail?
Is the overlay asset licensed/platform-safe or marked temp-only?
